name: Jahanka
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Galtier 1980 classification note on Glottolog; OLAC lists no descriptive resources for jad

sources.note: No descriptive references; only Galtier 1980 (subclassification) and Ethnologue vitality (6a). Alternative names Diakhanke, Diakkanke, Dyakanke, Jahanque, Jahonque.

sources.citation: Vydrin, V.F. 2017. Mande jazyki. In: Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande. St Petersburg: Nestor-Istorija, pp.16-45.
sources.note: p.17: džaxanká is a variant of Western Maninka-Xasonka/Mandinka spoken by a dispersed clerical-trader group; p.28 'idiom džaxanka blizok k mandinka'. p.34 pan-Mande: 'Udarenie v bol'šinstve M.ja. otsutstvuet. Tam, gde ono možet byt' vydeleno (v častnosti, bamana), ego funkcional'naja nagruzka nevelika' (stress is absent in most Mande languages; where identifiable, e.g. Bamana, its functional load is small). Nothing Jahanka-specific.

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis. 2013. Le mandinka du nord-est de la Guinée-Bissau. Paper presented at Mandenkan-50, INALCO/LLACAN, Paris, 14-15 Nov 2013, 12 pp. (Glottolog ref 318141, linked to jaha1245 as 'Gabu of Kaabu... probably Jahanka')
sources.note: §3.3 'Les tons' (pp.3-5): two-tone system as in Middle Casamance Mandinka plus 'report du ton haut' (H-tone shift) as in central/eastern Gambia. Nothing on stress or accent. The words Jaxanka/Jahanka never occur; Creissels treats the Gabú variety as ordinary Mandinka, so the jaha1245 link is Glottolog's guess.

sources.citation: Sullivan, Terrence D. 2004. A preliminary report of existing information on the Manding languages of West Africa: summary and suggestions for future research. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2004-005, 34 pp.
sources.note: §4.10 'Diakhanka' (p.20) gives only classification and location (Touba, NW Guinea, to Kedougou; data = Long's wordlists via Bimson 1978). 'Tone systems' (p.24) is a pan-Manding statement: terrace tone, lexical and grammatical tone contrast. No stress/accent statement for Diakhanka or any Manding lect.

sources.citation: Galtier, Gérard. 1981. Problèmes dialectologiques et phonographématiques des parlers mandingues (résumé of the 1980 Paris VII thèse de 3e cycle). Mandenkan 1: 39-58.
sources.note: Image-only scan, scanned (eng model). Classification only: jaxanka listed among Long's Manding lects (p.45) and placed in the 'sous-groupe xasonka (y compris le jaxanka et le maninka du Sénégal oriental)' of Western Manding (p.47); orthography section discusses tone marking in general. No stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis. [to appear]. A sketch of Mandinka. In F. Lüpke (ed.), The Oxford guide to the Atlantic languages of West Africa. OUP. Preprint.
sources.note: Mandinka (mand1436), not Jahanka; §2.4 Tone: two tones H/L, contours = sequences, downstep; no stress statement. Kept as nearest described variety.
Stubs; no phonology; cite only Ethnologue and Sullivan 2004.

sources.citation: Diallo, Abdourahmane. 2014. Language contact in Guinea: The case of Pular and Mande varieties. (TIAS 36.) Köln: Rüdiger Köppe, 422 pp.

sources.note: The only work anywhere that announces a phonological description of Jaxanka (Part I, contrastive phonology/morphology of Kakkaɓe, Jaxanka, Garanke); Glottolog's only Jahanka-tagged post-1990 source. Best chance of a tone/stress statement.

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis & Pierre Sambou. 2013. Le mandinka: phonologie, grammaire, textes. Paris: Karthala.
